name: ALICE+ (ours: meaning matching and facts)
source: elizita tier 4: the A.L.I.C.E. rules, plus matching by meaning with a small in-browser sentence model (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Apache-2.0), fact memory after Bruce Wilcox's ChatScript, and DOCTOR as the last resort.
about: Every rule system so far fails the same way: if you phrase something in a way nobody wrote a pattern for, it falls through to a generic catch-all. ALICE's 50,000 patterns still miss "my mum drives me mad".

This tier keeps all of ALICE's rules, but when only a catch-all fits, it asks a small neural model (about 23MB, running in your browser) which of ALICE's 22,000 fixed patterns is closest in meaning. The model turns each sentence into 384 numbers; sentences that mean similar things get similar numbers. If the closest pattern is close enough (similarity at least 0.6), ALICE answers that pattern instead. The workings show the match and its score.
If nothing is close enough, it hands the sentence to DOCTOR (the extended set), which looks for a keyword. Only if DOCTOR finds none does ALICE's catch-all reply.

It also remembers facts the way ChatScript bots (Bruce Wilcox, Loebner Prize 2010, 2011, 2014) do: tell it "my sister is called Ann" or "I have a dog called Rex", then ask "what is my sister's name?" or "what do you know about me?".
The model only picks which rule to use. Every reply is still written by a human rule author, and every step is visible.
